From your installed MEGALODON environment, start the local HUD. It checks tool presence at launch and works even before you have a data store. Companion tools are optional.

Open local HUD ↗

The local link works after launch on this computer. This hosted page does not test or connect to your machine.

python -m megalodon hud
First launch or need help?

Activate the virtual environment where MEGALODON is installed, then run the command. Keep that terminal open. Stop with Ctrl+C. Use Tools & consoles inside the local HUD; no report export or cloud login is required.

If the command is unavailable, review and install the HUD update first. An empty HUD does not start a sensor or generate data.

LOCAL READINESS REPORT

Bring a presence check into view

Open a bounded report generated on your Linux host. It stays in this page's memory and is never uploaded. An executable found on PATH does not establish compatibility, service health, or permission to run it.

Delivered in PR #241. On main@5583ac1 or later, run python -m megalodon readiness > megalodon-readiness.json. This checks executable presence only; it does not start a tool or establish compatibility.

DATA EXCHANGE · CONTRACT ONLY

Threat context and SIEM/SOAR boundaries

Three planned local handoffs improve interoperability without adding a live feed, cloud sender, credential, scheduler, or response path.

No runtime
STIX 2.1Offline threat context

Operator-supplied completed file, checksum-bound and capped at 16 MiB, 4,096 objects, and 32 nesting levels.

  • Preserve markings and provenance
  • Patterns remain inert text
  • No TAXII, fetch, attribution, or action
ECS · OCSFLocal SIEM projection

Future versioned ECS 9.5.0 and OCSF 1.9.0 views write only to a new bounded local file.

  • 10,000 records / 16 MiB maximum
  • No payload or event.original
  • No collector, credential, or network delivery
SOARInert handoff

A future provider-neutral record can describe review state while remaining incapable of delivery or response.

  • Destination not configured
  • Zero attempts; status not attempted
  • No endpoint, webhook, playbook, or host action

Contract fixtures are design evidence only. They do not prove parser safety, SIEM compatibility, delivery, threat coverage, or production acceptance. Review draft PR #264 ↗

      SAFETY MEMBRANE

      Trust membrane

      Autonomy stops before authority.

      A detection or advisory is evidence for review—not proof of malicious activity and never permission to change a host.

      Security review ↗
      01

      Metadata only

      No packet payloads or payload-derived hashes enter the core event model.

      02

      Loopback by default

      The read-only dashboard stays on 127.0.0.1:8787; there is no write API.

      03

      Local core operation

      The local core requires no cloud account. This hosted Site uses hosting/sign-in services; external setup links leave the Site.

      04

      Plan, do not apply

      Firewall proposals are inert. Live application remains explicitly refused.

      05

      Bounded local AI

      The optional client allows one bounded loopback request with no action authority. The separately operated model process is not confined by those client checks.

      06

      Finite evidence

      Implemented operations have documented bounds. The Suricata 512 MiB logical store ceiling is not a whole-disk or retention budget; retention remains operator-owned.

      Evidence flow

      One-way by design

      1. 01Bounded inputJSONL or a supported bounded adapter
      2. 02Fixed detectionSYN flood, port scan, DNS tunneling
      3. 03Atomic evidenceAudit ledger and terminal receipts
      4. 04Read-only reviewLocal dashboard and private reports

      Where the bytes live

      Tracked source vs. runtime-only storage

      Quoted from docs/storage-layout.md ↗. Cloning this repository creates only the left lane; the right lane exists only after an operator runs the named command.

      Tracked in git

      • config/*.tomlTyped defaults and the fixed detection-rule reference
      • contracts/*/v1/Inert schemas and accepted/rejected fixtures
      • megalodon/reference/*Pinned IANA snapshot and synthetic evaluation corpus
      • site/dist/This static console mirror; no process reads it at runtime
      run a command →

      Runtime-only, gitignored

      • data/megalodon.dbAudit ledger; 256 MiB default high-water stop
      • captures/, logs/Operator-authorized adapter input, never created automatically
      • offline-runs/One mode-0700 report-set directory per analysis run
      • --suricata-db <path>Operator-selected store; 512 MiB logical ceiling

      No command shares one path across stores. Each keeps its own owner-private directory and mode checks, so one store's failure or migration cannot touch another's.
